First, we substitute $u={x}^{2}+3.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,⟹\,\text{d}u=2x\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to \infty $ when $x\to \infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={x}^{2}+3$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $3$ | $\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{54x}{({x}^{2}+3)^{4}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{27}{{u}^{4}}\,\text{d}u
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{54x}{({x}^{2}+3)^{4}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{27}{{u}^{4}}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{\infty }27{u}^{-4}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{3}^{a}27{u}^{-4}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{[-9{u}^{-3}]}_{3}^{a} \\  & =-9\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[{u}^{-3}]}_{3}^{a} \\  & =-9\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }[\frac{1}{{a}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{3}^{3}}] \\  & =-9\cdot (0-\frac{1}{27}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
